name: Grade 6 T1: Responsible Technology and E-Waste
description: Internet Day vocabulary, reliable information, recycling, reuse, repair, e-waste, and sustainable habits.

words.definition: Protected from harm, risk, or unsafe online choices.
words.example: A safe internet habit is keeping passwords private.

words.definition: Able to be trusted because it is accurate or dependable.
words.example: Students should use reliable sources for facts.

words.definition: A planned message or project that tries to inform or persuade people.
words.example: The class made an Internet Day campaign about privacy.

words.definition: A visual message that uses text and images to share an idea.
words.example: The poster showed one rule for safe internet use.

words.definition: A visual that explains information using icons, short text, and data.
words.example: The infographic gave three tips for reducing e-waste.

words.definition: Something a person can do to help or solve a problem.
words.example: The campaign included one action step: recycle batteries safely.

words.definition: To process used materials so they can become new materials or products.
words.example: Some old electronics can be recycled at a collection center.

words.definition: To use something again instead of throwing it away.
words.example: A working keyboard can be reused by another student.

words.definition: To fix something so it can work again.
words.example: Repairing a cable can keep it out of the trash.

words.definition: Electronic waste, such as old devices, cables, batteries, or computer parts.
words.example: An old phone becomes e-waste if it is no longer used.

words.definition: A piece of technology, such as a tablet, computer, phone, or robot.
words.example: The device should be handled carefully.

words.definition: A part that stores energy and powers a device.
words.example: Batteries should not be placed in regular trash.

words.definition: A place where trash is buried or stored.
words.example: Keeping e-waste out of landfills helps protect the environment.

words.definition: The natural world around us, including air, water, land, plants, and animals.
words.example: Responsible technology choices can help the environment.

words.definition: Able to continue without wasting resources or harming the environment too much.
words.example: Repairing devices is a more sustainable habit than replacing them quickly.

words.definition: Putting items into groups based on what they are or what should happen to them.
words.example: The class practiced sorting items into reuse, repair, recycle, or e-waste.

words.definition: A place where people can bring items to be recycled or handled safely.
words.example: Old batteries can go to a collection center.

words.definition: Material that is thrown away or used carelessly.
words.example: Reusing a charger reduces waste.

words.definition: Something a person does regularly.
words.example: Turning off unused devices is a helpful habit.

words.definition: Knowing about an issue and understanding why it matters.
words.example: The project raised awareness about e-waste.

words.definition: Making careful choices that protect people, devices, and the environment.
words.example: Responsible technology use includes recycling old electronics correctly.

words.definition: A short piece of advice that helps someone do something better.
words.example: The slide included a tip about repairing devices before replacing them.
